decisive_items: recurrent episodes of abdominal pain, bloating, and obstipation, alternating with intermittent diarrhea
exploratory laparotomy “showed no mechanical cause of the obstructions.”
CT scan showed small-bowel dilation (approximately 23 mm in diameter) consistent with obstruction
response.rationale: Recurrent obstructive symptoms without a mechanical cause, with chronic small-bowel and colonic dilation, indicate chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction; R6 is the specific chronic form, while R5 is the broader term.

rejected.why: Weight loss and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency are secondary to chronic obstruction/malabsorption, not short bowel syndrome; no resection or shortened bowel is described.
Endoscopy showed no celiac disease and a gluten-free diet produced no improvement, directly contradicting it.
Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies are nonspecific and explained by intestinal stasis/malabsorption; no lymphangiectasia features are provided.
Alcohol history is present but symptoms began after cholecystectomy and persisted after alcohol cessation, making liver disease an unlikely primary cause.
